sentences.en: I trust myself to make the best decision with what I know now.
sentences.zh: 我信任自己，能根据目前所知做出最好的决定。

sentences.en: A big misconception or myth that we tend to believe as humans is that there is one best decision for us to make at every single turn.
sentences.zh: 作为人类，我们往往容易陷入的一个巨大误解或迷思，就是在每一个转折点上，都存在一个对我们来说最好的决定。

sentences.en: And if we are to carefully observe and analyse the environment, all the context, all the information that we have, we will be able to discern what that decision is.
sentences.zh: 如果我们仔细观察和分析环境、所有的背景以及我们所拥有的所有信息，我们就能够辨别出那个决定是什么。

sentences.en: And it's that decision that will unlock our dream life.
sentences.zh: 正是那个决定将开启我们的梦想生活。

sentences.en: To take that kind of further, that means that there is this perfect path through life almoSt.
sentences.zh: 进一步说，这意味着生命中几乎存在着一条完美的道路。

sentences.en: And we can obtain that perfect path by making the correct choice at every single point where we need to make a choice.
sentences.zh: 而我们可以在每一个需要做出选择的节点上做出正确的选择，从而获得这条完美的道路。

sentences.en: Do you kind of see the impossibility of that?
sentences.zh: 你大概能看出这有多不可能吧？

sentences.en: Because that's really what it is.
sentences.zh: 因为事实确实如此。

sentences.en: It's impossible.
sentences.zh: 这是不可能的。

sentences.en: It's improbable.
sentences.zh: 这是微乎其微的。

sentences.en: Making the most perfect decision is not actually something that we can always do because we don't always have the information that hindsight kind of provides.
sentences.zh: 做出最完美的决定其实并不是我们总能做到的事，因为我们并不总是拥有事后诸葛亮那种视角所提供的信息。

sentences.en: What we tend to forget is that there really is never a perfect choice.
sentences.zh: 我们往往忘记了，其实根本没有所谓的完美选择。

sentences.en: Otherwise, it wouldn't be a decision, right?
sentences.zh: 否则这就不能叫决定了，对吧？

sentences.en: Like the word decision means to resolve some kind of competition between two juxtaposed and perhaps equally good outcomes or options or equally bad outcomes and options.
sentences.zh: 就像“决定”这个词的意思，是为了解决某种在两个并置且可能同样优秀的结果或选项、或者同样糟糕的结果和选项之间的竞争。

sentences.en: I like to think about it this way.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这样想。

sentences.en: If you had to choose between two choices on a menu and one choice was your favorite meal ever and you know it's cooked deliciously and it's only $10 and the other dish
sentences.zh: 如果你必须在菜单上的两个选项中做出选择，其中一个选项是你最喜欢的美食，你知道它烹饪得美味无比，而且只要 10 美元；而另一个菜品

sentences.en: is a food that you're allergic to surrounded by other foods you don't like and it's out of your budget, the choice is actually quite easy.
sentences.zh: 是你过敏的食物，周围还环绕着其他你讨厌的食物，并且超出了你的预算，这个选择其实相当简单。

sentences.en: So it's not really a decision, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这其实算不上一个决定，对吧？

sentences.en: A decision only emerges when we feel torn by two alternative outcomes that have very similar pros and cons and the reason we feel stuck in those moments
sentences.zh: 只有当我们面临两个有着非常相似优缺点、让我们感到纠结的备选结果时，决定才会出现，而我们在那些时刻感到卡住的原因

sentences.en: is that we don't want to regret not choosing the right one.
sentences.zh: 是我们不想后悔没有选择正确的那一个。

sentences.en: What we're battling is perfectionism.
sentences.zh: 我们在与之对抗的是完美主义。

sentences.en: Of course, it is perfectionism.
sentences.zh: 当然，这就是完美主义。

sentences.en: You probably already guessed that but it's also our desire, maybe even our need to be in control and to have some assurance that it's all going to turn out okay
sentences.zh: 你可能已经猜到了，但这也是我们的欲望，甚至可以说是我们对掌控感的需要，以及对一切都会好起来的某种保证的渴望，

sentences.en: which is quite honestly something that no one can really give us you're just going to have to see for yourself and that's scary but it's also really exciting
sentences.zh: 老实说，这是任何人都无法真正给你的，你只能自己去经历看看，这很吓人，但当你细想时，这也 realmente 令人兴奋，

sentences.en: when you think about it because if you knew the outcome of every single decision that you were ever going to make from now until the day you died what's the point
sentences.zh: 因为如果你知道从现在到你死去的那一天你将要做的每一个决定的结果，那么活着的意义是什么呢？

sentences.en: of living your life?
sentences.zh: 说真的，如果没有一点兴奋感和一点惊喜，但有时又伴随着各种可能性，

sentences.en: Genuinely, what is the actual point of waking up and going forward without a little bit of excitement and a little bit of surprise but sometimes the possibility
sentences.zh: 去纠结于“如果……会怎样”以及各种替代假设，这其实是一个令人恐慌的心理环境，

sentences.en: and grappling with the what-ifs and the alternative hypotheticals it's a scary you know, mental environment to be in and so we don't see it in the same way
sentences.zh: 所以我们不会像我刚刚描述的那样看待它。

sentences.en: that I was just describing it.
sentences.zh: 我们并不认为它是令人兴奋的，而且在渴望做出完美选择的过程中，我们最终牺牲了一些东西。

sentences.en: We don't see it as exciting and in our desire to make the perfect choice we do end up sacrificing a few things.
sentences.zh: 平静就是其中之一。

sentences.en: Peace being one of them.
sentences.zh: 行动则是另一个。

sentences.en: Action being the other.
sentences.zh: 我所说的这种特定类型的“不作为”有它自己的名字，你可能听说过，它叫决策麻痹或选择过载，它解释了当我们被所有的可能性以及所有潜在的“如果”压倒时，

sentences.en: This specific kind of inaction that I'm talking about it has its own name you've probably heard of it it's called decision paralysis or choice overload and it explains what happens
sentences.zh: 我们的脑海里会发生什么——如果结果是这样呢，但如果结果是那样呢？

sentences.en: to our brain when we feel overwhelmed by all the possibilities and all of the potential what-ifs what if it turned out this way but what if it turned out that way
sentences.zh: 你大概能明白我的意思了。我们本能地会认为，拥有更多选项会让我们感到更自由、更解放，但事实似乎恰恰相反。

sentences.en: kind of see where I'm going with that we would think naturally that having more options would make us feel more free and more liberated it seems that it actually does the opposite.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈我有史以来最喜欢的研究之一，这是一项关于后悔的研究。

sentences.en: I want to talk about one of my favourite studies ever of all time and it's a study that was done on regret.
sentences.zh: 后悔真的是“当我没有完全的信息时，我该如何信任自己”这个核心问题所在，因为我们真正在担心的是：

sentences.en: Regret is really at the heart of this whole question of how do I trust myself when I don't have full information because what we're really worried about is
sentences.zh: 如果我做了决定又后悔了怎么办？

sentences.en: what if I make a decision and I regret it?
sentences.zh: 所以这项研究发表于近二十年前，但其中的发现在今天依然振聋发聩。

sentences.en: So this study was published almost two decades ago but the findings still ring so very true.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这项研究发现：比起“行动”，你更可能对“不作为”感到后悔。

sentences.en: Basically what this study found is that you are more likely to regret inaction than action.
sentences.zh: 在这个研究项目中，这些研究人员一次又一次地发现，那些他们交谈过的、在生活中感到最后悔的人，并不是因为某一个决定，

sentences.en: Time and time again across this research project these researchers found that those who they spoke to who had the most regret in life it didn't come from one decision it was not
sentences.zh: 不是因为某个单一的决定甚至多个错误的决定加剧了他们的后悔，而是因为他们由于太害怕

sentences.en: a singular decision or even multiple wrong decisions that heightened their regret it was regret from times when they had stayed stagnant because they were too scared
sentences.zh: 而选择停滞不前所带来的后悔——为了逃避不适感而停留在同一个地方，停留在明知不适合自己的同一份工作、同一段关系、同一个城市，

sentences.en: to make a choice they had stayed in the same place to avoid discomfort stayed in the same job stayed in the same relationship that they knew wasn't right for them the same city
sentences.zh: 那里的人不好、没有机会、让他们感到孤独，最终他们开始怨恨过去的自己，不是因为做出了某种选择，而是因为缺乏选择，

sentences.en: where there were bad people where there weren't opportunities where they felt lonely and eventually they came to resent their past self not for a choice but for a lack of choice
sentences.zh: 因为缺乏做决定的勇气。

sentences.en: for a lack of decision making
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在所有决策中对完美的错置渴望所付出的代价，它最终夺走了我们的快乐。

sentences.en: this is what the misplaced desire for perfection in all decisions costs us it ends up costing us our happiness so this is the first takeaway of the day if you are stuck
sentences.zh: 所以这是今天的第一个要点：如果你在做某事和不做某事之间卡住了，永远选择去做。

sentences.en: between doing and not doing something always choose to do it and with that I want you to know that choosing to live in perfectly choosing to make a choice even if you're not sure
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我希望你知道，选择不完美地生活，选择做一个决定——即使你不确定它是否正确——

sentences.en: if it's the right one it's actually going to give you so many more experiences so many more options to learn than you would obtain from just trying really hard
sentences.zh: 实际上会带给你比你费尽心思去做出一个正确选择所能获得的、多得多的经历和学习选项。

sentences.en: to make one right choice the second thing to note when we talk about making the best decision is that as humans research has shown that we are pretty bad at predicting
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论做出最好的决定时，需要注意的第二件事是，作为人类，研究表明我们其实很不擅长预测未来什么会让我们快乐或不快乐，

sentences.en: what is going to make us happy or unhappy about the future due to something called effective forecasting where we tend to think about our emotions as being more heightened
sentences.zh: 这是由于一种叫做情感预测的现象，我们倾向于认为自己在未来的情绪会被放大

sentences.en: or stronger in the future so either we're going to be so much happier incredibly happy if everything works out the way we wanted to or we're going to be truly devastated
sentences.zh: 或者变得更强烈：要么如果一切都如我们所愿，我们会超级开心、不可思议地快乐；要么如果事与愿违，我们会感到真正的崩溃。

sentences.en: if they don't so really what we are what we are stuck between is two extremes and that means that the stakes feel especially heightened what actually happens though
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，我们所陷入的是两个极端，这意味着风险感觉格外高昂。

sentences.en: when we make a decision when we get to our future regardless of what the outcome was we actually tend to return to a pretty stable emotional state fairly quickly after good or bad
sentences.zh: 然而，当我们做出决定、迈向未来时，无论结果如何，在好事或坏事发生后不久，我们其实往往很快就会恢复到一个相当稳定的情绪状态。

sentences.en: things happen so a study from
sentences.zh: 所以，来自澳大利亚迪肯大学的一项研究发现，

sentences.en: Deakin University here in Australia found that actually we overestimate the intensity and the duration of how long our happiness but also how long our misery is going to last
sentences.zh: 实际上我们高估了我们的幸福感以及痛苦感会持续的强度和时间。

sentences.en: what we are really good at though is being resilient and adapting to our circumstances we are highly adaptable creatures so even if you may think that it's the wrong decision
sentences.zh: 不过，我们真正擅长的是保持韧性并适应环境，我们是高度适应性的生物，所以即使你可能认为这是一个错误的决定，

sentences.en: most of the time you can still progress and find a way out it's also not like once you've made a decision you are locked into that decision for life you can change your mind
sentences.zh: 大多数时候你仍然可以前进并找到出路。而且，这也不是说一旦你做了决定，你就被终身锁定在这个决定上了，你可以改变主意。

sentences.en: you are allowed to change your mind also I always pose this hypothetical to people who have found themselves

sentences.en: regretting past actions or past choices I get so many messages from people saying
sentences.zh: 在为过去的行为或选择感到后悔的人提出这样一个假设，我收到过太多人的私信说：

sentences.en: I'm so upset at myself for doing this I feel like
sentences.zh: 我对自己做了这件事感到非常难过，我觉得

sentences.en: I've completely ruined my life I feel like I can link everything back to that time five years ago how do you know that that choice didn't save you from an even worse fate
sentences.zh: 我彻底毁了我的生活，我觉得我可以把一切都追溯到五年前的那段经历。你怎么知道那个选择没有让你免于更糟糕的命运呢？

sentences.en: how do you know that this actually wasn't the better outcome you can't and the chances are you're coping with it better than what a previous version of you would have thought
sentences.zh: 你怎么知道这其实不是一个更好的结果呢？你无法知道，而且很有可能你现在应对得比过去的你所想象的要好得多。

sentences.en: you could cope with so if we can't ever truly know what is going to make us happy or how things are going to work out how do we still make the best decisions
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们永远无法真正知道什么会让我们快乐，或者事情将如何发展，我们该如何做出最好的决定呢？

sentences.en: because it is important to still put some thought into it well what it comes down to is self-trust I love self-trust it is one of my favorite concepts but basically what it means
sentences.zh: 因为花心思去思考仍然是很重要的。归根结底，这取决于自我信任。我非常喜欢自我信任，它是我的最爱概念之一，但它基本上意味着：

sentences.en: is that you trust your ability to interpret the information you have now but you also trust your future self to handle whatever comes their way you are not so focused on trying
sentences.zh: 你信任自己解读目前所拥有的信息的能力，但你也信任未来的自己能够应对接下来发生的任何事情。你不再专注于试图

sentences.en: to make grand predictions instead you go forward with the information you have currently available to you and you also go forward with an attitude of forgiveness and grace
